overview.title: What each technology still needs
overview.lede: Escape Velocity is an open atlas of technologies on their way to maturity: where each one stands, the target that would make it useful, the physical limit behind that target, the gaps in between and the other technologies it waits on. Every number has a source.
overview.statCards: evidence cards, {verified} verified by a curator
overview.distanceText: The headline metric of each technology: how far the best demonstrated value is from the target, in orders of magnitude. Open a technology for the conditions and the evidence behind each value.
overview.noHeadline: No headline metric has both a current value and a target yet.

about.title: About
about.description: What the atlas is, its model, how to use its data, how to cite it and how to contribute.
about.heading: About the atlas
about.lede: Escape velocity is the speed at which a rocket stops falling back. A technology has one too: the point where it works well enough, cheaply enough and reliably enough to carry on by itself.

modelItems.text: is a capability with a measurable target, a statement and a scope.
has three numbers: the best value demonstrated so far, the target with its rationale, and the physical limit where one exists.
are classified by type, layer and severity. A gap held open by another technology points to it.
carry every number: the source, a verbatim quote, the conditions and a class (established, reported, extrapolation, speculation).

about.dataJson: {file}: the whole atlas in one file, with gap sizes, dependents and citations ({format}).
about.dataLlms: {llms} and {full}: the atlas for language models.
about.dataMcp: An MCP server for agents, in {file}: technologies, gaps, dependencies, bottlenecks, evidence and literature search.
about.citeText: Cite the atlas version you used: this page shows version {version} ({date}). The citation metadata is in {cff}. Data is under CC0 1.0, text under CC BY 4.0 and code under Apache 2.0.
about.contributeText: One sourced number is a real contribution. Every change, from a person or an agent, is a pull request reviewed by a person. See {link}.
about.rolesText: Each domain has moderators and each tracked technology has curators. They review the changes to what they look after, and only they mark an evidence card as verified. How the roles work, and how to take one, is in {link}.
about.alanMachineText: {link} is an open-source book about a hypothetical supercomputer at the physical limits of computation. The atlas shares its metrics and its kinds of claim, and links each technology to the pages that discuss it.
about.outOfScope: Out of scope: weapons, dual-use research of concern, surveillance aimed at people, investment advice and medical advice.

contribute.title: Contribute
contribute.description: How to add a sourced number, challenge a value, propose a technology or translate the atlas, with or without git.
contribute.heading: Contribute to the atlas
contribute.lede: One sourced number is a real contribution. You do not need to know the whole atlas, and you do not need git: a form on GitHub is enough.

whatItems.text: a paper, dataset or report with a number that updates a current value.
a current value, target, limit, readiness level or gap you think is wrong, with your source.
one the atlas should track, or a dependency that has no page yet.
a wrong or missing translation, or an offer to translate into your language.

contribute.whatSource: The source is what matters most. A number without a source cannot enter the atlas; a number with one, even a single one, can.
contribute.formsText: Each form opens on GitHub and needs only an account. It asks for what a reviewer needs, and the moderators of the domain triage it.

report-evidence.name: Report evidence
report-evidence.text: a source with a number that updates the atlas.

challenge-value.name: Challenge a value
challenge-value.text: a value you think is wrong, with your source.

propose-technology.name: Propose a technology
propose-technology.text: a technology or dependency the atlas does not have.

translation.name: Translation
translation.text: a wrong or missing translation, a glossary term, or an offer to help.

contribute.discussions: Ideas that are not a proposal yet, and questions about the atlas, go to {link}.
contribute.prText: If you can use a terminal, you can make the change yourself. It needs only Python 3.11 or later.
prSteps: Fork the repository on GitHub and make a branch.
Edit the TOML of a technology or an evidence card, starting from the templates.
Run the generator and the check; the check says what is missing.
Open a pull request and fill in its template.
A curator or moderator of what you changed reviews it, and a maintainer merges it.
contribute.rules: The step-by-step guide and the rules every pull request follows, from the evidence rules to the titles and the sign-off, are in {link}.
contribute.roles: To look after a technology, a domain or a language, see {link}.
